environment.placement: One Node 24 process hosted the Hub, 1000 SDK clients and Vitest; Redis 7.4.11 ran on the same host over loopback.

baseline.firstPatchPrototype: Timed out after 300 seconds with 1000 reactive observers; no successful result.

assertions: Each observer reconstructed the same exact 1000-entry FIFO line
Initial snapshots and subsequent batched changes converged
One post-measurement authority read verified the exact 1000-entry FIFO line
No full queue read or queue frame was used during admission

implementation: The server broadcasts a small queue invalidation across Hub instances and reads the full line only on a Hub with interested viewers. Refreshes coalesce, duplicate lines are suppressed, and append/remove batches use versioned patches. The SDK stores patches incrementally and materializes a public array only when queueFor is read. The measured Redis path uses an expiry index and a strictly increasing score for same-millisecond FIFO admissions. The final code gates the indexed path behind CLAIM_QUEUE_INCREMENTAL_READY=1 so the first mixed-version deployment repairs old writers' entries before enabling fast admission.
limits: One synthetic run per final mode; these are not latency percentiles.
Sequential admissions, one Hub process, loopback WebSockets and Redis, synthetic authentication and fence minting; no production database or cross-host network latency.
End-of-run RSS combines the Hub, all SDK clients and the test runner; it is not peak server-only memory.

A full line requested by every observer still requires substantial fanout: 229 MB of queue frames and 1.56 GB combined RSS in this fixture. A full 1000-entry array is materialized when each observer reads queueFor.
The benchmark does not execute Rust/FUSE or live model agents. The Rust authority and production deployment were not changed.
